cards.explanation: The answer is True, friends. The people gathered in such large numbers that there was "…no more room, not even outside the door…" (Mark 2:2) I've seen a full cookie jar, but that crowd had it beat. And Jesus is right in the middle of it, speaking the word to them.

The answer is that they open the roof and lower him down on his mat, friends. They were unable to get through the crowd, so "…they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat." (Mark 2:4) When the front door is blocked, these four go for the ceiling. I admire that kind of stubborn.
The word is faith, friends. "When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic…" (Mark 2:5) The text says their faith, and Jesus saw it. Then He spoke to the man on the mat.

What Jesus says first is, "Son, your sins are forgiven." (Mark 2:5) I bet a few people in that house expected something else first. Jesus starts with forgiveness, friends, and He says it right to the man on the mat.

The scribes are thinking that He is blaspheming, since only God can forgive sins, friends. They are thinking in their hearts, "Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?" (Mark 2:6-7) Their question is a good one, and Jesus is about to answer it.

Jesus knew it in His spirit, friends. "At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves." (Mark 2:8) Nobody had to tell Him anything, because He knew it right away. Then He asked them, "Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?" (Mark 2:8)

The reason Jesus gives is that they may know He has authority to forgive sins, friends. He says, "But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins..." (Mark 2:10) "…Son of Man…" is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). So the reason He gives is His authority to forgive sins.

The answer is False, friends. The man does not wait for help. "…immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all." (Mark 2:12) The text says nothing about waiting or a helping hand. I'd have needed a minute and a cookie, but he stood right up.

The words are astounded and glorified, friends. "…they were all astounded and glorified God…" (Mark 2:12) The man walked out in front of them all. What they saw sent their praise to God, and they said, "We have never seen anything like this!" (Mark 2:12)
